description: Unit (maintenanceJobFanout): renew-microsoft-calendar-webhooks is in the EE schedule catalog and the job registry, is tenant-scoped, and its run calls renewMicrosoftCalendarWebhooks with the tenant id.
Integration (DB-backed): the tenant selector returns only tenants with an active Microsoft calendar provider (excludes tenants with none, with only Google, or with only inactive Microsoft providers).

Integration (DB-backed, Graph mocked or msgraph emulator): a provider with an expired subscription is recreated by renewMicrosoftWebhooks, webhook_subscription_id and webhook_expires_at are updated, a health row is written, and an event changed in Outlook during the gap is applied through the catch-up delta sync.
Integration (DB-backed): an ordinary renewal inside the look-ahead window extends webhook_expires_at and does not run a catch-up sync.
Unit: the extracted delta sync resets and refetches when the stored deltaLink is rejected, and persists the new deltaLink; processMicrosoftWebhook produces the same result as before through it.
Unit: isResourceNotFoundError is true for a 404 status or ResourceNotFound code and false for an unrelated error whose message contains '404'.
Integration (DB-backed): with two providers in one tenant, a token failure on the first records a failure in calendar_provider_health and the second is still renewed.
Unit (setupSchedules): the legacy calendar-webhook-maintenance-schedule is deleted and not recreated; the temporal-workflows package builds with the workflow and activity removed.

Unit (parity): the test fails when a recurring registered handler name has neither an EE schedule nor an exemption, and passes with the current set; the CE catalog test still asserts the calendar jobs are absent in CE.
